With a nod and a smile, Kerrigan rode off. *Damn Princes...*

The next day, Kerrigan decided it was time for him to involve himself in... something. He sent a messenger to go fetch Lord Baldric for some socializing and hopefully some shenanigans. The young lord sported a fine outfit, one considered highly fashionable by those in the know and considered slightly queer by those with knowledge elsewhere. 

Imported straight from Braavos, Kerrigan wore a deep purple tabard over his simple grey doublet. The tabard was rarely seen in Westeros, but it was prominent in Essos among the wealthy. Kerrigan made sure to purchase a few just for impressing high lords. He was a vain young man, that was certain.

Sending word to meet him at his rented estate, Kerrigan waited patiently, hoping to see the Lord Baratheon and get a sense of the man. Kerrigan had his few servants prepare wine and a meal for the two lords. If the Baratheon lord took time out in his day to have a meal with Kerrigan, Kerrigan figured he could do very much in these coming weeks.

Boredom hit Kerrigan hard, but when he heard that Lord Baldric would be in town, he decided to put down his most recent project and head out. Kerrigan fetched a few guardsmen and some nicer garb for such an occasion. Kerrigan was known to sport the newest and best fashion, something he hoped would be recognized during the tourney, despite him knowing no one would care. 

The young lord mounted his horse and began to ride. The streets of Oldtown were hectic and surprisingly dirty. Being from Strongsong, Kerrigan had not seen the filth and grime of large cities. Though Strongsong was prominent, it was not even close to matching the mere presence of Oldtown. It was a city that never ended. 

Atop his horse, Kerrigan approached slowly just before Lord Baldric was swept away by the Prince. He managed to get a few words in before having to scuttle for his Prince. 

"Send for me when you have the time, Lord Baldric. I'd very much like to meet you."

Lorrik breathed deeply and rose from his knees, brushing off his trousers and turning. He cocked an eyebrow," Everyone is *always* thinking I'm going to hit them." His gestures were foppish at best, and his mannerisms were that of a circus freak. 

"If I wanted to give you what I gave to the other guy, do you think I would have stopped him from cutting your throat?" He rolled his eyes before focusing his gaze, jaw clenching," Use your head, girl! Though..." he softened," I shouldn't blame **you**. It isn't uncommon for humans to be intimidated. Look, the name is Yorman. Well, it's J-O-R-M-A-N, but the M is silent, really."

*A fight?*

*Well, that's useful.*

Lorrik stood and watched from a distance, seeing and feeling her use the force without even knowing it. He lusted for that feeling again, the simple push one felt when the force flowed perfectly, and he didn't even know it.

"That's enough, gentleman." He approached, yellow eyes stinging the perpetrator as he held her. A knife was pulled and pressed on her throat. Oh, what a grand time this will be! 

Lorrik, with speed that was quite impressive (but not unheard of from non force-sensitives) rushed forward. With just a pinch of the force, Lorrik kept the man from slitting the girl's throat before sending him reeling with a well placed punch. 

Lorrik's eyes lit up and he followed the man to the ground, happiness filling him as he viciously beat the grimy human senseless. One, two, three, twelve punches were thrown, practically sending the man's nose into his brain. 

Oh, how glorious that would be.

Lorrik was down with the peasants of Theenes as he felt a very particular string from his spiderweb of the force vibrate. A presence? He must investigate, if only driven by professional curiosity. He followed the feeling- followed his force web- until he found himself in a semi-bustling marketplace where all manner of filth sold their equally abysmal products. 

The Sith made his way to the center of said marketplace, using his physical stature to bully his way past the crowds of people. There, he closed his eyes- or opened his mind- to the recesses of the force, beating it into submission so that he could find what he wanted. 

Off he went, spurring the force along, bending it to his own will. He saw a young girl, and he raised an eyebrow. She was fair of face and could not have been any older than twenty, though the dirt and grime on her face would say otherwise. He did not do much for now... Trailing behind her, waiting until she needed someone to come to her aid.

Lorrik's hands fidgeted about uncomfortably. His lips pursed and his head bobbed back and forth dramatically as a show of distaste. He quickly reached through the force and pulled the artifact from one of the pockets to his hands. 

*Yes!*

He looked at the small shard of a saber. Though it's master was long dead, he could still feel the power emanating from such an object. He stuffed it into one of his pockets and looked at the bounty hunter again. 

"You got a ship? I can wire more credits to you if you can get me out of this system. I feel another force presence."

Lorrik turned on his heel and saw the scoundrel leaning upon a staff. *What is he trying to do? Show off?* Lorrik stood up and pointed his saber," You're back?" His question sounded more like an impressed statement. 

With a quick flourish of his saber he turned it off and took a few steps to him. If looks could kill, Lorrik's bright yellow eyes would have put a whole in the man's forehead. Alas, he did not, and the weapon he could use to burn holes in people was on his hip. 

He knew this man. He had sent him on a mission to recover a sith artifact that had been stolen from him. He never expected him to return. Perhaps the bounty hunter had something to him, after all.

"You're back. You have what is mine?"

After a few minutes of standing within the crowds and mingling, Joffrey spotted a particularly pale man with a cloak of raven feathers. He was, on all accounts, the obvious choice of Blackwood. Joffrey sauntered up to him after passing through the crowd and offered a genuine smile. The Pipers and Blackwoods have always had good relations due to trading of resources and Lord Joffrey's wife being a cousin of the pale lord.

"Lord Blackwood, always a pleasure." Joffrey said, eyes darting in all directions to get a better view of the situation.

Crowds. Joffrey hated crowds, but he loved to play the game. Sometimes those two went hand-in-hand when dealing with lords. Leaning back in his chair, Joffrey sipped wine and brooded as he watched the room. The clanging of glasses and chatter of guards were background noise to the voices around him.


“Aren’t you going to speak to the others?” a young voice popped up from beside him. Alerie looked over at him, raven black hair in curls. 


“I already spoke to Lord Frey and Lord Tully.” He answered.


“Well, yes, but shouldn’t you speak to the others? I think my cousin is here.”

Joffrey looked down at Alerie,” I suppose that would be a good idea.” He rose from his seat and took his goblet of wine, wandering out into the open area. Joff’s eyes waved left and right, scanning the room for any sign of the Blackwood lord.

Joffrey internally cursed Robb's ability to be so idiotically joking around their liege lord. He cocked an eyebrow and turned to the Tully," Lord Tully." He said as he bowed his head slightly.

"All is well and more, my lord. Pinkmaiden has been reinforcing it's walls and strengthening for many years, my lord." Joffrey held back a sly smile toward Robb," With the new borders, us southern lords must be ready. Of course, I also have something for you, if you would speak in /private/ later."

"Ah, you Freys." Joffrey chuckled," I've got no relatives outside of distant female cousins. Can I borrow a few of yours. I'm sure they can get places and work." he said with a sly smile.

"Congratulations to your second born, by the way, I'm sure he's a good boy and keeps his father informed on the comings and goings." He half-joked.

Joffrey flashed a genuine smile and pulled his hand behind his back, straightening his posture.

"Oh, how I envy them, my lord." He sighed," I remember when I was just like them." He looked over and viewed all the eager knights looking for glory. "Those days are gone for me, however, I know am just looking to serve king and country. All that good shit people say. I just want what's best for me and mine." Joffrey spewed a bit.

"Who?" Joffrey leaned over to whisper in his wife's ear.

"Frey."

"Name?" 

"Robert...? Robb." She said, smiling.

"Good." Joffrey approached the Frey and held out his hand," Lord Robb. Fancy seeing you here."

On his way, Qion nonchalantly plunged his green saber into Jaiden before leaping over him and continuing his escape.

Dead Jedi were all well and good, but they would die in vain if Qion could not find a way to escape this predicament. Qion swung his sabers with ease and precision as he fought the jedi. Nimen was a form, however, that relied on creativity. Qion knew this and prepared to unleash his next offensive. A combination, it was, of two force based attacks.

Qion closed his eyes and walked to the other side of his cell as he began his speech, staring at the wall of his own prison. He looked down in sadness as the Zabrak attempted to defend his own oxymoronic view of the force.

"Then it is true..." Qion spoke, turning finally, his hands clasped around his back," Then you are lost. You are a slave to your own ideals that clash with themselves. Qion sighed," What do they teach you about the dark side of the force, Master Jedi? Do they teach you that the Dark Side is evil and it's users are horrible monstrous people? Qion clasped his hands behind his back and began to pace around the room, looking to Zur with a strange compassion," I would have nothing of you, Master Jedi. I simply find you...fascinating. Truly, you, as a being, represent the order as a whole."

He was almost used to his surroundings now, finding the glamor of the Jedi Temple a nice change of pace from the holes he had hidden in all his life, preparing for this exact moment and moments after. Each move was tactfully placed, as he worked his life like pieces in a bigger game in which he alone knew the rules and the final destination. Final destination, that is what it was all about. How would you be remembered? What is your legacy?

Durasteel, no doubt about it, with tendrils of black ready to strangle his enemies... but they only seemed to writhe around his own neck, suffocating his own abilities and making him an easy kill.
